import AppKit

/// The volume line on the timeline (road map "audio" AP8a, spec §11
/// AU-81…AU-84): every clip with sound draws its envelope — the plan's ramps
/// through `VolumeLines`, on `VolumeScale` — over its waveform; a press on it
/// drags the level in force, ⌥-press adds a point. The model is
/// `VolumeLine.swift`.
///
/// Extensions in a file of their own, as the speech duck's line is
/// (`TimelineView+DuckCurve.swift`): `TimelineView.swift` is frozen at wiring
/// and keeps one call in `hit(at:)` and one arm in each gesture phase.

/// One clip's line as drawn and hit: its rect, the scale on it, the ramps,
/// the polyline's vertices and the points (action ends naming the volume).
struct VolumeLineGeometry {
    let rect: CGRect
    let scale: VolumeScale
    let ramps: [PlanRamp]
    let vertices: [CGPoint]
    let points: [CGPoint]
}

extension TimelineContentView {
    /// The shortest line rect drawn (AU-81).
    static let volumeLineMinHeight: CGFloat = 12
    /// How far from the line a press still takes it (AU-84).
    static let volumeLineReach: CGFloat = 3

    /// The line on `clip` in lane rect `rect`: the audio region with its top
    /// raised to the action lane's bottom where they overlap, at least 12 pt
    /// tall, on a clip with sound that is not a nest clip and has an audio
    /// segment in the plan; nil otherwise. The drawing and the hit test both
    /// read this, so they cannot disagree.
    func volumeLineGeometry(
        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, rect: CGRect, owner: TimelineView
    ) -> VolumeLineGeometry? {
        guard clip.source.nestID == nil, owner.hasAudio(clip),
              let ramps = owner.volumeLines?.ramps(for: clip.id)
        else { return nil }

107:- **It replaces the volume** rather than multiplying it, so pressing it a second time changes nothing (the second press beeps). A measured volume within 0.05 dB of the clip's own is left as it is, so a clip measured through its processing doesn't move by a rounding either.
174:The shapes are always the clip's own setting, even with an action selected. It travels with the clip when you move it, and it stays at the edge when you trim. Where a fade in and a fade out overlap, or a fade is longer than the clip, the two multiply, which gives a dip in the middle rather than a jump.
180:- The fade length snaps to whole frames and can't be longer than the clip.
207:With **Clip Length**, ducking follows the clip's length on the timeline, not whether anyone is talking. The other audio stays lowered for the whole length of the ducking clip, through pauses, and comes back up only after the clip ends. You can therefore see exactly when ducking applies by looking at the timeline. If the attack is longer than the clip, the level never fully reaches Level, and the release starts from wherever it got to.
219:- **Overlapping duckers multiply.** Where two ducking clips overlap, their levels multiply: two at 50 % give 25 %.
479:When the shot before was detached too, its sound sits on the same track as this one's, so a lead would overlap it and become a cross dissolve. **Drag the sound to a track of its own first**, then trim it: on its own track, the lead overlaps nothing.
499:When two clips on one track overlap with a transition, the transition can also crossfade their sound. Turn on **Crossfade Audio** in the clip's Transition section. The crossfade keeps the combined loudness steady across the overlap. See [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).
540:- **They multiply what's on the track.** A clip at 200 % on a track at −12 dB plays at −6 dB. Two pans multiply too: a clip panned left on a track panned left leans further left.
571:- **Approximate in the preview.** The preview plays a track's sound in more than one piece where its clips overlap (a crossfade, or a nest's tracks), and it runs the compressor and limiter on each piece separately, so the pieces can add up past a track limiter's ceiling while editing. Measured on two clips at −1 dBFS crossfading under a limiter at −6 dBTP, the preview's true peak was 5.2 dB over the ceiling; the export held it. The Loudness Meter says "approximate" while any track has a compressor or limiter.
643:- **It corrects drift.** If two clocks run at slightly different rates, the recorder slowly falls out of sync over a long take. When the clips overlap for at least 60 seconds, Frame Job measures that drift and corrects it by playing the clip at a slightly different speed, at most 0.2 % from ×1. The correction is a plain resample, so the pitch moves very slightly with it. Drift is left alone when it is under 5 ms over the overlap, when it is too small to tell from no drift (under three times its own uncertainty), or when the speed it needs is more than 0.2 % from ×1. The corrected speed appears in the clip's Speed section (for example ×1.0004), with Keep pitch turned off. The command shows no drift figure of its own; that speed is where the correction shows. Like any clip at a speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, the corrected clip's sound is rendered in the background, so it is briefly silent in the preview after the correction, and again after each trim, split or speed change of it (see [Speed](speed.md)); an export waits for it.

33:## The Clip tab's pinned block
35:With a clip selected, three things stay pinned at the top of the Clip tab while its sections scroll underneath: the selection header, the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) and the sub-tabs.
48:The strip under the action lane splits the Clip tab into **Text**, **Shape**, **Graphic**, **Picture**, **Color**, **Sound** and **Clip**. It shows only what the selection can use, and sections that don't apply are absent, not greyed out.
73:## Selection follows to the Clip tab
75:Clicking a clip on the timeline or the canvas moves the inspector to the **Clip** tab, even if the clip was already selected. A selection that changes any other way, such as a paste, <kbd>⌘A</kbd> or an agent, moves it only from **Media** or **Document**.
96:On the Clip tab, a section you've never clicked starts closed, except Transform, a text clip's Content, a shape's Shape and a graphic's Properties. Every Media and Document section starts open.
98:If every section on a Clip sub-tab would be shut, the first one you haven't folded yourself opens by default. A section you closed yourself stays closed.

3:description: Drag an action's band or type its Start, Length and Curve to change when it happens, or remove it and leave the clip in place.
9:You can change when an [action](/motion/actions/) happens, how long it takes and how it eases, by dragging its [band](/motion/action-lane/) or typing in the action lane. Removing an action leaves the clip where it is.
14:  where={['The action band on the timeline', 'Clip tab ▸ action lane']}
20:  alt="The top of the Clip tab with action 1 selected. The lane shows the action's band across the middle of the clip. Under it, the detail row has a Start field reading 00:00:00:15, a Length field reading 1.00 s, a curve glyph, a Curve pop-up set to Linear and a trash button."
25:Drag the body of a band, on the timeline or in the Clip tab's action lane, to move the action within its clip. The pointer is an open hand over the body, and a dashed outline marks where the band started.
27:When you let go, the action is selected and the playhead sits at its new end, or one frame short of it when the action ends with the clip. The whole drag is one undo step, **Move Action**.
31:Drag either end of a band to move that end of the action. Each end's grip is its outer 5 pt. The grips appear when you hover over the band, and the pointer becomes a left-right arrow over them.
33:The action stays selected and the playhead goes to its new end, as with a move. The whole drag is one undo step, **Resize Action**.
35:A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips and only moves. [Zoom the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) in, or type a [length](#type-a-start-length-or-curve).
37:## Where a drag stops
39:A band drag snaps to whole frames and keeps the action at least one frame long. It stops at the neighbouring actions and at the clip's ends. It doesn't snap to the playhead or to other edits.
41:If Frame Job wouldn't allow a position, the band stops there and shows no message. A Speed action stops where the clip would run out of media, for example.
54:A key the property doesn't have, or a value of the wrong kind, is refused. The answer gives the dotted path, array indices included, and for a bad value, the value you sent. Nothing is dropped, corrected or clamped on the way.
